newsitem.title: FINLAND: Catering truck for Clinton but no national anthem.
newsitem.headline: Catering truck for Clinton but no national anthem.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton arrived on Thursday for a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in somewhat unusual style -- in the back of an airport catering truck and unable to stand for the national anthem.
Wheelchair-bound because of a leg injury, Clinton could not walk down steps from his Air Force One plane to the airport tarmac in Helsinki.
Instead, he was taken off the presidential jumbo jet by a truck belonging to the Finnish national carrier, Finnair .
In freezing winds, officials struggled to lay out a red carpet for Clinton and then had to nail it down to the tarmac.

The catering truck, with a compartment on a hydraulic lift, appeared alongside Clinton's plane. A door opened and the truck's compartment was raised, then lowered, then raised again as Secret Service agents swarmed around the vehicle.
Twenty-five minutes after Clinton landed at 0950 GMT, there was still no sign of the president.
Finally, the door of the catering truck opened. An official carrying a pair of crutches preceded Clinton, who was rolled out in a wheelchair, smiling sheepishly.
Clinton descended on a ramp to the red carpet and rolled forward to shake hands with his host, Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari.
A white van with tinted glass appeared and the U.S. president was wheeled into it and whisked off in a convoy of limousines, minibuses and an ambulance.
There was no band to play the U.S. national anthem.
A Finnish Foreign Ministry official said: "We assume it's because he is in a wheelchair and it would not be proper if he can't stand."
